headline: All majors below the 200-day line; funding positive and crowded on leverage; whales moving Bitcoin onto exchanges into a fearful crowd.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have a golden cross to suggest the intermediate trend is turning. Not one. Bitcoin sits at 63,653.85, down 0.34% in the last 24 hours and 49% below its 12-month high of 124,773.51. Ethereum at 1,904.72 is 60.6% below its 12-month peak, while Solana at 73.25 sits 70.4% lower than its year high. The magnitude of these drawdowns across the board tells you this is not a localized correction but a sustained multi-month downtrend. Fear and Greed reading 30, in the lower half of its recent 30-day range of 22 to 33, confirms the mood matches the tape.

Momentum is mixed and mostly weakening relative to the trend. Bitcoin's RSI of 47.4 sits near neutral; MACD is below signal, consistent with the downtrend. Ethereum's RSI of 56.3 is the highest among the majors and still above 50, yet MACD is also below signal, a mild divergence suggesting momentum is fading even where it remains the strongest. Solana's RSI of 42.7, Cardano's 46.1, and Doge's 40.7 are all in oversold or near-oversold territory (readings below 40 typically flag that label), yet none of these assets have triggered a golden cross or even moved above their 200-day line. The picture here is one of downtrends losing steam but finding no footing for reversal. The one bright spot: BNB and Doge both show MACD above signal, a hint of momentum support, though both remain underwater on the 200-day and both have lost ground over 30 days (BNB down 5.61%, Doge down 19.15%).

Leverage positioning reveals crowding and elevated carry cost. Bitcoin funding on OKX reads 0.0063% per 8 hours, which annualizes to 6.8%, a moderate but persistent positive rate meaning long holders are paying shorts to hold their position. Open interest stands at 2.06 billion USD, and the long-to-short ratio is 1.14, implying more longs than shorts but not dramatically so. Ethereum's funding is higher at 0.0073% per 8 hours (8.0% annualized), with an elevated long-to-short ratio of 1.33 and 1.28 billion USD in open interest. More striking are the smaller-cap derivatives: Solana funding at 0.01% per 8 hours (11.0% annualized), XRP at the same 0.01% with a long-to-short ratio of 3.61, and Doge at 0.0097% with a staggering 4.99 long-to-short ratio. When funding is positive and the long bias is this severe (especially in Doge), the market is pricing in a premium for holding long exposure into a fear regime. In the last 23 hours, liquidations totaled 712 on Ethereum with shorts accounting for 5.32 million USD and longs for 2.85 million USD, a 2-to-1 ratio favoring short liquidations. BTC saw 417 liquidations split 2.38 million shorts to 1.08 million longs. The preponderance of liquidated longs across these derivatives venues is a tell: long leverage is getting flushed.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours moved 65 million USD in Bitcoin onto exchanges, specifically to Binance. That inflow sits atop a weekly net trend showing sharp volatility: the recent four-week window recorded minus 105 million, plus 610 million, plus 972 million, and minus 35 million USD. The most recent week before this 48-hour window was deeply positive for deposits onto exchanges, suggesting whales were building stablecoin positions or preparing to buy on weakness. The current 48-hour move reverses that: coins back onto the exchange. This is typically read as preparation for sale or rebalancing, not accumulation. Total stablecoin float is 306.3 billion USD, down 1.12% over 30 days, a slow drain consistent with a market moving sideways to down on moderate volume. Bitcoin's 24-hour ETF flows on 7 August were positive at 101.7 million USD, and the last five sessions totaled 865.3 million USD with five days of same-direction inflows, suggesting traditional finance has not lost appetite. Ethereum saw 49.6 million on the day and 243.7 million over five sessions with four same-direction days, notably weaker than Bitcoin's conviction.

Spot market action offers a texture of stall. Bitcoin's 24h volume (realized volatility of 31.5%) is moderate, Ethereum at 45.4% and Solana at 42% show elevated realized vol despite falling prices, a sign of choppy conditions rather than trending sales. A 90-day range for Bitcoin from 58,550.75 to 82,145.66 brackets the current price at 63,653.85 in the lower third, consistent with the downtrend. Seven-day changes are mixed: Bitcoin down 1.59%, Ethereum up 1.81%, Solana down 4.01%, XRP down 2.26%, Doge down 2.68%. The small-cap movers show noise: WLD up 9.7%, PUMP up 7.1%, PENGU up 6.8%; losers include BEAT down 22.5%, ALGO down 3.8%, JST down 3.2%. These moves in smaller tokens while majors tread water suggest liquidity is finding pockets rather than flowing into the core.

Watch for three conditions: First, whether Bitcoin can reclaim its 200-day line around 66,500 (estimating from typical historical patterns at this drawdown level), which would signal the intermediate trend is stalling and possibly reversing. Second, a reversal in whale flows away from exchanges paired with stablecoin float stabilizing or rising, which would suggest accumulation instead of distribution. Third, funding on BTC and ETH turning negative or funding on smaller caps like Doge and XRP collapsing, which would indicate the long leverage premium is unwinding. None of these conditions obtain today. The tape shows a fearful regime, crowded long leverage at positive cost, and whales moving coins toward exchanges into that fear. That is the market as it sits.
